questions.question: Which of the following measures was NOT introduced by the French revolutionaries to create a sense of collective identity (sentiment of nationhood)?
options: Continuation of the traditional royal white flag of the Bourbon monarchy
The notions of 'la patrie' (the fatherland) and 'le citoyen' (the citizen)
A new French tricolour flag replacing the former royal standard
Adoption of a centralized administrative system with uniform laws for all citizens
questions.explanation: The French revolutionaries replaced the royal white standard with a new French tricolour flag; they did not continue the royal flag.

questions.question: In pre-unification German states, what was the 'elle'?
options: A gold currency coin issued by Frankfurt
A measure of textile cloth whose length varied from region to region
A customs duty tax imposed at river tolls
A weight standard for agricultural grain
questions.explanation: The 'elle' was a traditional unit of length used for measuring cloth. In Frankfurt an elle was 54.7 cm, in Mainz 55.1 cm, in Nuremberg 65.6 cm, and in Freiburg 53.5 cm, illustrating pre-Zollverein commercial complexity.

questions.question: In his famous 1882 Sorbonne lecture 'Qu'est-ce qu'une nation?' ('What is a Nation?'), Ernst Renan argued that a nation is:
options: A territory defined strictly by common language, race, and religion
A daily plebiscite based on a long past of endeavours, sacrifice, and devotion
A piece of land conquered and held through military force alone
An imperial dynasty ruled by divine right monarchy
questions.explanation: French philosopher Ernst Renan criticized the view that a nation is formed solely by language, race, or geography, arguing instead that a nation is a large-scale solidarity and 'a daily plebiscite' founded on collective past sacrifice and present consent.
